# Independent Tiled package consumer

This small technical sample consumes the published `tiled` package from a different Go module
and generated SDK package than Willowbrook. It uses the regular Go compiler;
Willowbrook uses TinyGo. The 16×10 orthogonal map has 24×32 cells and a 16×24
atlas with margin/spacing, all eight Tiled GID flip combinations and a standard
450/550 ms tile animation. The patterned atlas is generated by `cmd/author` to
make orientation visible; it is not replacement village artwork.

From the CLI repository root, using published SDK 0.0.19 selected by this fixture:

```sh
mise run author-tiled-room
mise run build-tiled-room-web
mise run check-tiled-package-web
```

SDK 0.0.19 requires Go 1.27.3 for the game compiler. Set `KARTY_GO` to that
compiler when needed. The CLI installs and verifies the published SDK bundle
and its matching host for the web build.
The pure shared package builds independently with the repository toolchain.

WASD/arrows pan continuously; R resets the camera. Click/touch recenters through
ordinary Karty `Camera2D.ScreenToWorld`. The small `src/backend.go` maps shared
sprite states to this game's own generated SDK. Asset generation calls the same
shared PNG importer as Willowbrook and writes an ordinary level manifest.

The browser check executes actual WASM, observes sprite residency/animation and
bounded protocol batches, verifies portrait touch projection and captures the
live framebuffer. Reports live in `dist/validation/tiled-package`. Chromium
SwiftShader and synthesized input do not qualify physical-device performance.
The fixture pins the published archive URL and SHA-256 in `karty.toml`.
Normal builds restore it automatically into ignored `.karty/packages/tiled`.
The archive check copies this consumer to a fresh temporary project, imports
the same published archive and builds it there.

```sh
mise run check-tiled-package-archive
# Use webDirectory from dist/validation/tiled-package/archive/report.json:
mise run check-tiled-package-web -- --directory /tmp/your-fixture/game/dist/web --label archive
```

The archive task checks the imported checksum and Go module resolution inside
the fresh project's archive store. It does not publish the package.

Map JSON is a build input selected by `tiled.compile` in `karty.toml`. The
processor emits binary `.karty/processed` resources; the cartridge decodes KTM1
records and does not embed the editable map or tileset. Source edits rebuild
these resources during normal `karty build` and `karty dev`.
